entries.name: Vshell_DbaLoadWrapper
entries.description: Identical in shape to Vshell_PanelLoadWrapper but for .DBA bitmap-array resources (e.g. "dba\mis_icon.dba"). Confirms both file kinds funnel into the same generic VshellClassItem_LoadItem loader.

entries.name: Vshell_PanelLoadWrapper
entries.description: (path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, asserting (src\shellmap.cpp line 0x5f) that it opened, loads one class item from it with VshellClassItem_LoadItem(stream, 0), asserting (line 0x62) that one loaded, destroys the stream and returns the item. Any class item: ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded loads dfn\map.dfn, a GLFont, with it. Vshell_DbaLoadWrapper is its sibling for .DBA files.

entries.name: ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded
entries.description: shellmap.cpp. Lazy-loads mis_icon.dba, mapshp.dba, and map.dfn into globals (guarded by null-checks), asserts on failure, sets a screen-state byte to 0. Confirmed via direct string references to the three literal filenames.

entries.name: ShellMap_ReleaseResources
entries.description: shellmap.cpp teardown counterpart to ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded -- destroys the 3 loaded resources (calls each object's vtable+0x18 destructor) and nulls the globals. Confirmed the only other reference to ShellMap_DfnPanelPtr in VSHELL.EXE besides the loader -- the loaded DFN panel object's contents are never read, only destroyed.

entries.name: ShellMap_Constructor
entries.description: ShellMap::ctor (vtable &PTR_FUN_004721b0). Opens data\mission.str and data\maplabel.str as independent string tables, then calls ShellMap_LoadScriptDat. Confirmed via assert string. The object is the briefing's map; see docs/retail/shell/mission-map.md.

entries.name: ShellMap_Dtor
entries.description: (map, flags): ShellMap's destructor (vtable 004721b0, RTTI ShellMap, 0x3c5 bytes): restamps the vtable, passes the object at +0x4e to 0045dbf0 and then runs its virtual destructor, frees the arrays at +0x52, +0x56, +0x5e, +0x62, +0x6e and the +0x72 six-byte records' buffers at +0x5a and the array itself, deletes +0x66, runs StringTable_Dtor on +0x219 and +0x1b7 and Map_Dtor, and Mem_Delete's the map when flags bit 0 is set. ShellMap_Build destroys the previous map with it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042424a; tools/scripts/es2_naming.py rtti VSHELL 004721b0

entries.name: ShellMap_ResetViewAndClear
entries.description: (map): copies the full view (+0x187/+0x18b/+0x18f, which ShellMap_FitBounds sets) into the camera position +0x12/+0x16 and altitude +0x1a, runs ShellMap_Clear between Map_PushContext and Map_PopContext, and sets the byte +0x186 to 1. A grep of the decompile for +0x186 finds two writes, ShellMap_Constructor's 0 and this 1, and no read. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: ShellMap_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: shellmap.cpp. The briefing map's reader for data\script.dat -- a SECOND, independent reader of the same 13-block structure WriteScriptDatFile (0041ac54, VSHELL) writes and DBSim_LoadScriptDat (00424308, DBSIM) also reads. Confirmed byte-for-byte identical block order/strides to both, differing only in which fields it keeps vs seeks past (e.g. keeps row12/row14/row15 blocks in full for UI display, where DBSIM keeps only 1 field or discards entirely). Not an independent or map-rendering-only format. See docs/retail/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: ShellMap_LoadZone
entries.description: Loads dat\zone%d.dat (keeps int32[2] cell shift at +0x104, int32[3] height scale) and dba\zone%d.dba through HeightGrid_Load into the map's HeightGrid (DAT_00472258).

entries.name: ShellMap_ReadSquadHeader
entries.description: shellmap.cpp (source line 0x1f5). The only VSHELL function found that parses data\player.mec (Career_SaveSlot and Career_LoadSlot copy it whole); it takes just the two leading int16 -- the player entry index and the squad size -- before closing it and opening data\mforms.dat for formation layout. No VSHELL reader of the rest of player.mec, including the trailing weapon-unlock table, was found by a literal-reference sweep.

entries.name: ShellMap_FitBounds
entries.description: Full view: centre of the widened block-1 bounds and the altitude fitting both halves in the viewport; also the altitude limit +0x3bd.

entries.name: ShellMap_FitSquad
entries.description: Squad view +0x193/+0x197/+0x19b: the same fit over the squad's positions widened by 250000.

entries.name: ShellMap_SkipIntro
entries.description: Moves the intro state +0x172 to 0x11 (the closing zoom) when it is below 0x12.

entries.name: ShellMap_Paint
entries.description: Map vtable slot 0: camera clamp, then clear, relief, grid and bounds, path, bases, nav markers, squad.

entries.name: ShellMap_Clear
entries.description: Fills the viewport with 0x10; busy-waits 10 ticks during the intro's first paint.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintRelief
entries.description: Stretches the relief bitmap (+0x3c1) over the bounds widened by 100000 through GLBitmap_DrawStretched.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintGrid
entries.description: Grid lines in 0x0f every 200000 through the projected origin; outside the first paint, the bounds outlined in colour 10 (Gfx_FillRect mode 4).

entries.name: ShellMap_IntroStep
entries.description: The intro state machine (+0x172, 20 states): hold, zoom to the squad, reveal the squad, pan along the nav path, zoom back. Timer is GetTickCount()>>4.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintPath
entries.description: Nav path in 0x0e; part-way through the intro only the line to the camera centre and a radius-3 pen.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintBases
entries.description: Bases shown by +0x1a (friendly non-zero, hostile == 1), mis_icon frame by type.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintIcon
entries.description: Icon at a world point: projected size below a threshold plots a pixel, below the frame height a scaled blit, else the frame.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintNavMarkers
entries.description: mis_icon frames 14+ at path points after the first, up to nine.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintSquad
entries.description: Squad icons, frame 3 for block-7 record 0 else 5, as many as the intro has revealed.

entries.name: ShellMap_CurrentLine
entries.description: Picks the mission.str line the intro has reached into +0x17e; the rest of its body is empty branches, so it draws nothing.

entries.name: ShellMap_BuildRelief
entries.description: Banded relief of the cells under the widened bounds: min(h,0x7f)/5 + 0xd1, two Gfx_BandedTriangle per cell, min(640/cols, 400/rows) pixels a cell.

entries.name: ShellMap_ClampCamera
entries.description: Caps the altitude at +0x3bd and keeps the centre half a viewport inside the bounds widened by 100000.

entries.name: ShellMap_ZoomOut
entries.description: Map vtable +8: altitude += 50000 when the clamp leaves it; then ShellMap_PanStepFor.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanWest
entries.description: Map vtable +0x14: pan x -= step when the clamp leaves the moved centre alone.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanEast
entries.description: Map vtable +0x18: pan x += step, same test.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanNorth
entries.description: Map vtable +0xc: pan y += step, same test.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanSouth
entries.description: Map vtable +0x10: pan y -= step, same test.

entries.name: ShellMap_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (_INIT_ entry at 00481004, pointer at 00481006), in an Eh_InitExceptBlock frame (00471ed0): GLBitmap_Ctor on g_ShellMapReliefBitmap (0048a2ef), then writes the int16s 00471e2f = 0xc000, 00471e31 = 0 and 00471e33 = 0. A grep of the disassembly for those three addresses finds these writes and no read. ShellMap_StaticDtor destroys the bitmap.

entries.name: ShellMap_StaticDtor
entries.description: Exit routine (_EXIT_ entry at 00481052, pointer at 00481054), frameless: GLBitmap_Dtor(g_ShellMapReliefBitmap (0048a2ef), 2), destroying the static bitmap without freeing its storage.

entries.name: AnimDisplay_Dtor
entries.description: AnimDisplay's destructor, the dtor its class record (0xa0 bytes, at 00427ba5) names: (display, flags): when display is not null, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, GLDisplay_Dtor(display, 0) for its DVDisplay base, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: TSLight_Dtor
entries.description: TSLight vtable 00472188 slot 0, the destructor (light, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, destroys the member at +0x1e with TSContext_Dtor(+0x1e, 2) and the light itself with TSContext_Dtor(light, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: TSSunLight_Dtor
entries.description: TSSunLight vtable 0047219c slot 0 (light, flags): when light is set, decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr twice (its own level and TSLight's), destroys the TSContext member at +0x1e with TSContext_Dtor(+0x1e, 2) and the light with TSContext_Dtor(light, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. ShellMap_Constructor builds the map's sun as one, with +0x16 = 1.

entries.name: StringTable_Ctor
entries.description: Clears a string table: buffer +0, cursor +4, length +8 and the group counters +0xc and +0xe. ShellMap_Constructor builds its table with it.

entries.name: StringTable_Dtor
entries.description: The string table's destructor, the dtor its class record (RTTI 'Strings', 0x10 bytes, at 00427cca) names: (table, flags) decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, StringTable_Free, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. ShellMap_Dtor runs it on the map's two tables.
entries.source: es2_classes.scan: the Borland class record's +0x28 destructor; VSHELL decompile

entries.name: StringTable_Load
entries.description: (table, path), assert file src\strings.cpp: opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, asserts it opened, reads it with StringTable_LoadFromStream, destroys the stream and returns that result. String-table reader: +0 content buffer, +4 cursor, +8 content length, +0xc int16 strings in the current group, +0xe int16 index within it. Layout of the file in docs/retail/formats/str-strings.md.

entries.name: StringTable_LoadFromStream
entries.description: (table, stream): reads the int32 content length into +8, allocates that many bytes (Mem_NewArray, asserting in src\strings.cpp on failure) at +0, reads the content into it and sets the cursor +4 to the start. Returns 1.

entries.name: StringTable_Free
entries.description: Frees a string table's buffer (Mem_DeleteArray) and zeroes the buffer, cursor, length and group counters.

entries.name: StringTable_PeekGroupCount
entries.description: Returns the byte at the cursor, the low byte of the next group's int16 count, sign-extended; 0 when nothing is loaded.

entries.name: StringTable_ReadNext
entries.description: (table, &text, &attributes): reads the next string. At the start of a group it takes the int16 count first. Stores a pointer to the text (after its int16 length) and, when attributes is non-null, to the attribute bytes after the count byte, then advances past both. At the end of a group it resets the group counters and returns 0; also 0 past the end of the content.

entries.name: StringTable_LoadGroup
entries.description: (table, texts, capacity, attributes): reads the next group's count, asserts in src\strings.cpp when capacity is positive but smaller than it, and fills texts[i] (and attributes[i] when that array is given) with StringTable_ReadNext, asserting on a short group. Resets the group counter and returns the count. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's StringTable_LoadGroup.

entries.name: StrTable_FirstString
entries.description: (table): the loaded .STR buffer (*table) + 4, the first entry's text past the group's int16 count and the entry's int16 length; 0 when the buffer pointer is 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Identical after normalisation to DBSIM's StrTable_FirstString (004539b0).
entries.source: VSHELL disassembly at 00428165; diff against DBSIM 004539b0

entries.name: StrTable_NextString
entries.description: (table, string): the string after the given one in a loaded .STR buffer -- steps over the text by its length prefix, the attribute count byte and its attributes, and the next entry's length -- or null past the buffer's end (*table + size table[2]). es2_xref finds no reference to it. Identical to DBSIM's StrTable_NextString (004539cc) after normalisation.

entries.name: StrTable_GetAttributes
entries.description: (table, string): the entry's attribute bytes -- string + its int16 length prefix (string-2) is the attribute count byte, and the result is the byte after it -- or 0 when the count is 0 or string lies past the buffer. es2_xref finds no reference to it. Identical to DBSIM's StrTable_GetAttributes (00453a08) after normalisation.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot8ReturnsZero
entries.description: Slot 8 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600): returns 0, so RasterDriver_OpenDisplay's slot-8 check of the bitmap header always passes. DBSIM's slot 8 is the same (0048a0c0).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 004281f4; table dump at 0047e600

entries.name: Driver3_OpenDisplay
entries.description: Slot 11 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600), which RasterDriver_OpenDisplay calls with (bitmapHeader, info): keeps the header at 00481834, allocates a row-offset table (base, then one offset per row) into info+0 (freeing the previous one, 0046d73c), takes the width and height from GLDisplay_OpenWithSize's one-shot overrides (0046d734, 0046d738, reset to -1) or else from the header, fills the rest of info (+0x24/+0x28 the header's own size, 8 bits, 256 colours) and sets the screen rect and origin globals. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0048a0c8.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 004281fb; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a0c8

entries.name: Driver3_Slot7NoOp
entries.description: Slot 7 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600): returns at once. RasterDriver_OpenDisplay and GLDisplay_SetAttribute call slot 7. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Driver3_Slot7NoOp (0048a218).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042837a; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a218

entries.name: Driver3_CloseDisplay
entries.description: Slot 12 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600), which RasterDriver_CloseDisplay calls: (info) frees the row-offset table at info+0 that Driver3_OpenDisplay allocated. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Driver3_CloseDisplay (0048a220).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042837f; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a220

entries.name: GLDisplay_OpenWithSize
entries.description: (display, bitmapHeader, width, height): stores width at 0046d734 and height at 0046d738 when not negative, GLDisplay_Open, then on success selects the display as the render target, sets its attributes +0x88 = 0 and +0x8c = 1 (publishing them when it is the current target), and sets its page offsets (0, 200, 400, 600 for kind 'VGA 8', zero otherwise). Driver 3's open routine (004281fb) takes the stored width and height once, in place of the header's, then resets them to -1. Display_Init and ShellMap_BuildRelief call it.

entries.name: Terrain_FillCellUntextured
entries.description: (vertices, count, shades): fills one view-space polygon for hgrid.cpp's cell drawer (00429dac, twice). Points Poly_ViewVertices at vertices and the ring at Poly_SequentialIndices with count vertices from 0, clears their Poly_VertexState and runs Poly_ProjectViewVertices; when it reports a vertex behind the near plane, Poly_ClipRingToNearPlane and, with g_ShadeMode at 2, Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithShade over shades. It then installs a brush at +0x22c of the context 0048e184 points to: with g_ShadeMode 2 mode 1 on the ramp 00472254 with the per-vertex shades, otherwise mode 0 with the colour (first shade << 16) | 0x4000000 | low word of 00472254; and PolyFill_Fill. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_FillCellUntextured (0046bb40), which uses ramp 2, looks the flat colour up through Palette_ShadeRampLookup and wraps the fill in a dummy drawable.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0046bb40

entries.name: Terrain_BindTextureBank
entries.description: (name): copies name into a 32-byte local, appends '.dba' (004722c5), loads it with Vshell_DbaLoadWrapper and stores what BitmapArray_PackToAtlas (0045d270) returns for it at g_TerrainTextureFrames (0048a310): BitmapArray_PackToAtlas (0045d270) places each frame of the bitmap array in an atlas page (Bitmap_PlaceInAtlasPage on AtlasPage_Root), writing one 0x14-byte descriptor {x0, y0, x1, y1, page} per frame. Terrain_ResolveCellTexture indexes the table. No caller found by es2_xref. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_BindTextureBank (0046bc98), which joins the name with the dba folder instead.

entries.name: Terrain_ResolveCellTexture
entries.description: (material, cx, cy, uvOut): one cell's texture corners for the hgrid cell drawer. material is an 8-byte record {frame, shift} (grid+0x11d + the cell's byte +0x19 * 8). With shift 0 the frame's 0x14-byte descriptor in g_TerrainTextureFrames gives u0, v0, u1, v1 (+0 to +0xc) as they are; otherwise u0 = (cx << shift) & 0xff, v0 = (cy << shift) & 0xff, u1 = u0 + (1 << shift), v1 = v0 + (1 << shift). Writes (u0, v0), (u0, v1), (u1, v1), (u1, v0) into uvOut and returns the descriptor's +0x10, the atlas page. Terrain_DrawCellRowRun calls it (es2_xref: one CALL, at 0042a9aa). The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_ResolveCellTexture (0046bcf4), which shifts by cellShift + shift - 13 and negates v.

entries.name: Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest
entries.description: (normal int16[3], point int32[3]): dot(normal, g_TerrainViewerPos - point) > 0. HGrid's cell drawer 00429dac calls it twice and 0042b019 once. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest (0046bd98).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; es2_naming.py match/diff against the DBSIM function named in the description

entries.name: HeightGrid_Ctor
entries.description: HeightGrid constructor (vtable 00472470 after the ClassItem 0047f834 and TSBase 0047f858 base vtables; RTTI name 'HeightGrid', 0x125 bytes): Rtl_VectorNew of 0x14 8-byte elements at +0x28, 00467ee4(+0xd0, 0x100) for the height offset table, zeroes +0xf0/+0xf4/+0xf8 and sets +0x104 = 10, +0x108 = 8. ShellMap_LoadZone calls it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042870b; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: HeightGrid_Dtor
entries.description: HeightGrid vtable 00472470 slot +0x18 (grid, flags): decrements *Rtl_DtorCountPtr, restores the vtable, frees the array at +0xec when set, decrements once more and runs TSBase_Dtor on the height offset table at +0xd0 (the VectorTable HeightGrid_Ctor builds there), then TSBase_Dtor(grid, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellSurface
entries.description: (grid, cx, cy): writes the 0x1c-byte cell's diagonal selector (+0x18) and both face normals (+8 near, +0xe far, int16[3] each) from its corner heights h00 (cx, cy), h01 (cx, cy+1), h11 (cx+1, cy+1) and h10 (cx+1, cy). Selector 1 when h00 + h11 == h01 + h10, both normals (h00 - h10, h00 - h01); 2 when h00 + h11 is the smaller, near (h01 - h11, h00 - h01) and far (h00 - h10, h10 - h11); 0 otherwise, near (h00 - h10, h00 - h01) and far (h01 - h11, h10 - h11). Both vertical components are (1 << grid+0x104) / grid+0x114, and all six are doubled. Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade calls it (es2_xref: one CALL, at 00428b66). The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_BuildCellSurface (0046bed8).

entries.name: Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength
entries.description: (v int16[3], length): halves all three components until Math_FastMagnitude3D fits under 0x7d01, then scales each by (length << 16) / magnitude through FixedMulQ16. 00428b2d calls it twice. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength (0046c138).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; es2_naming.py match/diff against the DBSIM function named in the description

entries.name: Terrain_BuildSurface
entries.description: (grid): Raster_SetModelTransform(0), then two passes over every cell row by row (1 << grid+0x100 rows of 1 << grid+0xfc cells, 0x1c bytes each from grid+0xec): Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade, then Terrain_BuildCellVertexShade. ShellMap_LoadScriptDat calls it on the shell's height grid (DAT_00472258) after ShellMap_LoadZone (es2_xref: one CALL, at 00424a48). The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_BuildSurface (0046c1dc), whose second pass is Terrain_CellSecondPassNoOp.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade
entries.description: (grid, cell, cx, cy): for a cell short of the last row and column, Terrain_BuildCellSurface and Math_NormalizeVec3ShortToLength(normal, 0x800) on both face normals (+8, +0xe); otherwise both normals become (0, 0, 0x800) and the selector is left as it is. Then bakes cell +0x14 = Light_ComputeShadeForNormal(+8, 0048a32d) and +0x15 = Light_ComputeShadeForNormal(+0xe, 0048a32d). Terrain_BuildSurface's first pass (es2_xref: one CALL, at 00428a98). The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_BuildCellSurfaceAndShade (0046c2ec).

entries.name: Terrain_BuildCellVertexShade
entries.description: (grid, cell, cx, cy): the vertex normal at cell +2/+4/+6 and its shade at +0x16. On row 0 or column 0 the normal is (0, 0, 0x800) and +0x16 keeps its value. Otherwise each component is a running halved sum, ((((a + b) >> 1 + c) >> 1 + d) >> 1 + e) >> 1 + f) >> 1, of this cell's near (+8) and far (+0xe) normals, cell (cx-1, cy-1)'s near and far, cell (cx, cy-1)'s near and cell (cx-1, cy)'s far; +0x16 = Light_ComputeShadeForNormal(that normal, 0048a32d). Terrain_BuildSurface's second pass (es2_xref: one CALL, at 00428af3). Terrain_DrawCellRowRun takes +0x16 as a corner's shade in g_ShadeMode 2. DBSIM's Terrain_BuildSurface runs Terrain_CellSecondPassNoOp in this place.

entries.name: HeightGrid_FromBitmap
entries.description: hgrid.cpp: the shell's copy of the zone loader's bitmap path -- one height byte per pixel, rows north to south, material rolls.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Load
entries.description: hgrid.cpp: loads data\mat0.dat, then a .dba through HeightGrid_FromBitmap or any other extension as the ASCII debug format.

entries.name: Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion
entries.description: (grid, view, polygon): installs the view's position (+4/+8/+0xc) as g_TerrainViewerPos and clears the model transform. With polygon 0: sets up a view volume (ViewFrustum_Ctor (00467614), ViewFrustum_Build (00467654)) for the range grid+0x108 << cellShift (+0x104), builds the square about the viewer with Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad, clips it with ViewFrustum_ClipGroundPolygon (00467ac4) (passing grid+0x10c and +0x110), sets grid+0x118 to whether a region is left and, when one is, stores its points in cells (>> cellShift) at grid+0x28 with count +0xc8 and pointer +0xcc. With polygon {count, points}: clamps each point to the grid's world extent, sets grid+0x118 when point 0's x is below point 2's and its y below point 1's, and on success shifts the caller's points to cells in place and uses them as the region (+0xc8 count, +0xcc pointer). On success both paths put the grid origin +0x1c through g_ModelToView, rotate the cell steps (1 << cellShift, 0, 0) into +4 and (0, 1 << cellShift, 0) into +0x10, and run HeightOffsetTable_SetScale(grid+0xd0, +0x10c, +0x114) and HeightOffsetTable_Reset. ShellMap_PaintRelief calls it (es2_xref: one CALL, at 00425883) with DAT_00472258, the map's camera and a four-point rectangle. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion (0046ca98), which writes the draw radius grid+0x10c from the terrain-detail option itself.

entries.name: HGrid_RenderAround
entries.description: (grid, position): hgrid.cpp's cell renderer, while grid +0x118 is set. Clears the model transform, installs a mode-0 brush at the context's +0x22c for the walk, takes the cell of position (+4, +8, shifted down by grid +0x104) and its byte +0x17, and walks the polygon at grid +0xc8 around it with CellWalk_Polygon, callback 00429dac. When that byte was set it calls HGrid_InvokeCellHook(grid, cellX, cellY) after the walk. Restores the brush. See docs/retail/polygon-fill.md.

entries.name: Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad
entries.description: (grid, polygon{count, points}): the square of half-side grid+0x108 << cellShift (+0x104) about g_TerrainViewerPos's x and y, clamped to the grid's world extent (origin +0xf0/+0xf4, size 1 << (+0xfc or +0x100 plus cellShift)). When the clamp leaves it empty, count = 0. Otherwise asserts (src\hgrid.cpp line 0x2cf) when the count on entry is below 4, sets count 4 and writes the corners (x0, y0), (x0, y1), (x1, y1), (x1, y0) as Point3I with z = grid+0xf8. Terrain_SetupVisibleRegion calls it (es2_xref: one CALL, at 004298d4). The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_BuildDrawRegionQuad (0046d220).

entries.name: Terrain_DrawCellRowRun
entries.description: (ctx, row, xFrom, xTo): the cell callback HGrid_RenderAround hands CellWalk_Polygon (stored pointer at 00429bdb); the grid is ctx+0x18 and the column step ctx+0xc. Builds the view-space corners of cell (xFrom, row) in HGrid_CellCorners from the grid origin +0x1c and the cell steps +4 (X) and +0x10 (Y), and draws each cell from xFrom to xTo by the step inline: adds each corner's HeightOffsetTable_Get(grid+0xd0, raw height); by the corners' third view-space components (c0 + c2 equal to, below or above c1 + c3) makes one quad in HGrid_CellPolyA or two triangles in HGrid_CellPolyA and HGrid_CellPolyB; and draws each triangle that Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest finds facing the viewer (normals +8 and +0xe). With DAT_00471874 0: Terrain_FillCellUntextured, the shade from Light_ComputeShadeForNormal below g_ShadeMode 2, or the corners' +0x16 in mode 2 (averaged with half the corner's height plus 0x1e when DAT_0047187c is set). With DAT_00471874 1: Terrain_ResolveCellTexture, Raster_SetVisibilityRange (0042026c)(grid+0x108 << cellShift), Raster_SetDepthFadeFromDistance(the nearest corner's depth), g_PerspectiveUseQuadraticFit = that depth > DAT_0047223c (25000), the baked +0x14/+0x15 in g_ShadeMode 1, and TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB when the depth is below DAT_00471880 * 2, else TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA. Then HGrid_InvokeCellHook. After the run, clears DAT_0048a32c when row is DAT_0048a324 and the run covered column DAT_0048a320. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_DrawCellRowRun (maybe_PaletteDirtyFlag (0046dcd8)) with Terrain_DrawCellQuad inlined.

entries.name: Terrain_HeightQuery
entries.description: (grid, point{x, y}): the ground height under a world point, in EAX. The cell is (x, y) >> grid+0x104; 0 outside the 1 << +0xfc by 1 << +0x100 grid. Corner heights are raw * grid+0x114 + grid+0x10c, interpolated over the triangle the point's cell-local offset falls in by the cell's selector +0x18 (2 and 0 split the cell along opposite diagonals, 1 is one plane through (cx, cy), (cx+1, cy) and (cx, cy+1)). No caller found by es2_xref. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_HeightQuery (0046e07c).

entries.name: Terrain_FaceNormalAt
entries.description: (grid, point{x, y}): a pointer to the int16[3] face normal of the triangle under a world point, or 0 outside the grid. The cell is (x, y) >> grid+0x104; with selector +0x18 2 it returns the far normal +0xe when the cell-local y is below the local x, else the near +8; with any other selector the far normal when local y exceeds the cell size less local x, else the near. HeightGrid_PickDrawCell calls it (es2_xref: one CALL, at 0042b1d6). The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_FaceNormalAt (0046e394).

entries.name: HGrid_InvokeCellHook
entries.description: (grid, cx, cy): when the cell's byte +0x17 (cells 0x1c bytes from the pointer at grid+0xec, rows of 1 << grid+0xfc) is non-zero, calls the hook at grid+0x121 with (cx, cy, that byte). HGrid_RenderAround and the cell drawer 00429dac call it.

entries.name: HeightGrid_PickDrawCell
entries.description: (grid, pos, radius): the cell an object at pos is drawn with. Starts from pos's cell ((x, y) >> grid+0x104); by the quadrant the viewer's cell (g_TerrainViewerPos, same shift) lies in, when pos is within radius of the cell's viewer-side edge on an axis it moves one cell toward the viewer on that axis, and undoes both moves when Terrain_FaceNormalAt gives a face that Terrain_FaceVisibilityTest finds turned away from the viewer. Off the grid it returns 0; otherwise it increments the cell's byte +0x17, writes x, y and that count into the 3-byte record HeightGrid_DrawCellRecord (0048a428) and returns it. No caller found by es2_xref. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's HeightGrid_PickDrawCell (0046e528) with HeightGrid_ClaimDrawCell inlined; DBSIM's also tests the visible region.

entries.name: HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch
entries.description: (grid): zeroes byte +0x17 of every 0x1c-byte cell from grid+0xec ((1 << +0xfc) * (1 << +0x100) cells), the per-cell count HeightGrid_PickDrawCell increments and HGrid_InvokeCellHook hands the grid's hook. No caller found by es2_xref. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's HeightGrid_ClearCellScratch (0046e840), which clears a separate byte array at +0xf0.

entries.name: Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest
entries.description: (grid, cx, cy, point, edge): whether the terrain along one edge of cell (cx, cy) is at or above point's z. Edge 0 takes corners (cx, cy) and (cx, cy+1), 1 (cx+1, cy) and (cx+1, cy+1), 2 (cx, cy+1) and (cx+1, cy+1), 3 (cx, cy) and (cx+1, cy), each raw * grid+0x114 + grid+0x10c. Returns false when z is above both, true when z is at or below the lower, otherwise whether z is at or below the edge height interpolated at point's offset along the edge (y for edges 0 and 1, x for 2 and 3). No caller found by es2_xref. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_EdgeCrossingTest (0047035c).

entries.name: Terrain_CellSurfaceIntersect
entries.description: (grid, from, to, arg4, cx, cy); the body reads arguments 1-3, 5 and 6. Where the segment from-to meets the ground in cell (cx, cy), in cell-local x and y and world z. Builds the near triangle's plane {+8 normal, d = -(h00 * nz)} and intersects it with Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect into Terrain_CellSurfaceHit (0048a42c); keeps the hit by selector +0x18 (1 always, 0 when local x + y is at most the cell size, 2 when local x < local y) and returns Terrain_CellSurfaceHit (0048a42c) with the cell origin added back. Otherwise, for selectors 0 and 2, tries the far plane (normal +0xe): for selector 0 with d from corner (cx+1, cy) and the segment moved one cell west, for selector 2 keeping the near plane's d; returns Terrain_CellSurfaceHit (0048a42c) on a hit, else 0. Selector 1 returns 0 on a miss. Sets the byte 004722c4 to 1 on entry. No caller found by es2_xref. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_CellSurfaceIntersect (0047068c).

entries.name: Terrain_ProjectFarEdgeAhead
entries.description: (grid, view): when the viewer's cell (view +4/+8 >> grid+0x104) is at least grid+0x108 cells from every grid edge, projects the point grid+0x108 << cellShift straight ahead along the view's heading (+0x14; Math_BuildRotation2D and Transform2D_ApplyToPoint about the viewer's x and y) at height grid+0x10c, through the transform at DAT_005d7fa0, Raster_Project and Raster_ToScreen, and returns its screen y; otherwise returns DAT_005d7ff4. No caller found by es2_xref. The hgrid.cpp counterpart of DBSIM's Terrain_ProjectFarEdgeAhead (00470910), which writes both screen coordinates to an out argument and uses distance 1000 near an edge.

entries.name: HGrid_SpanAddCell
entries.description: (grid, cx, cy): for a cell with 0 <= cx < (1 << grid+0xfc) - 1 and 0 <= cy < (1 << grid+0x100) - 1, widens row cy's span in HGrid_RowSpans to include cx and the range HGrid_SpanFirstRow..HGrid_SpanLastRow to include cy; ignores any other cell. HGrid_SpanAddOctants calls it eight times.

entries.name: HGrid_SpanAddOctants
entries.description: (grid, centre, a, b): HGrid_SpanAddCell on the eight points centre +/- (a, b) and centre +/- (b, a), each shifted down to a cell by grid+0x104. HGrid_BuildCircleSpans calls it.

entries.name: HGrid_SpanMeanHeight
entries.description: (grid): averages the raw height byte +0 of the 0x1c-byte cells over HGrid_RowSpans: rows HGrid_SpanFirstRow to HGrid_SpanLastRow + 1, the extra row reusing the last row's span, columns from each span's minX to maxX + 1. Returns sum / count. HGrid_BuildCircleSpans calls it (es2_xref: one CALL, at 0042bd24). The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's HGrid_SpanMeanHeight (00470bac), which bounds-checks the cell index.

entries.name: HGrid_SpanSetHeight
entries.description: (grid, height): writes height into the raw height byte +0 of every cell HGrid_SpanMeanHeight averages, then walks the spans twice more (rows HGrid_SpanFirstRow - 1 to HGrid_SpanLastRow + 1, columns minX - 1 to maxX + 1) with empty loop bodies. HGrid_BuildCircleSpans passes it HGrid_SpanMeanHeight's result (es2_xref: one CALL, at 0042bd2c), levelling the circle to its mean height.

entries.name: HGrid_BuildCircleSpans
entries.description: (grid, centre, radius): resets HGrid_RowSpans (all 0xffff), HGrid_SpanFirstRow (1 << grid+0x100) and HGrid_SpanLastRow (0), then rasterises the circle of radius about centre into per-row cell spans: HGrid_SpanAddOctants for (0, radius) and, stepping a by the cell size from the next cell boundary, for (a, radius * cos(asin(a / radius))) while a stays below that value. When HGrid_SpanFirstRow is below HGrid_SpanLastRow, levels the spanned cells to HGrid_SpanMeanHeight's result with HGrid_SpanSetHeight.

entries.name: HGrid_StaticInit
entries.description: Static initialiser (_INIT_ entry at 0048100a, pointer at 0048100c), frameless: Rtl_VectorNew of Terrain_DrawCellRowRun's scratch arrays: 8-byte points (Rtl_ReturnArg) x4 at 0048a34c, x4 at 0048a36c and x3 at 0048a38c, and Point3Is (0xc bytes, maybe_Point3I_Ctor) x4 at HGrid_CellCorners (0048a3a4), x4 at HGrid_CellPolyA (0048a3d4) and x3 at HGrid_CellPolyB (0048a404). The cell drawer keeps Terrain_ResolveCellTexture's corners in 0048a34c and the two polygons' UVs in 0048a36c and 0048a38c.

entries.name: HeightGridCell_ElementCtor
entries.description: (cell): returns cell; the LEAs of +2, +8 and +0xe are left over from inlined empty constructors of its three int16[3] vectors (the vertex normal and the near and far face normals). The per-element constructor HeightGrid_FromBitmap and HeightGrid_Load pass Rtl_VectorNew (pointers at 00428dbf and 00429346) for the (1 << grid+0xfc) * (1 << grid+0x100) cells of 0x1c bytes they store at grid+0xec.

entries.name: Sfx_Init
entries.description: (sfx, cacheLimit, fileCount, sampleCount): stores the cache limit at +0x18 (the bytes Sfx_Cache may hold, 0 for none) and the counts at +0x10 and +0x14, allocates the 0x21c-byte file table (+0x34) and the 0x28-byte sample table (+0x38) with every slot's +0 at -1, then opens the drivers through 0042d7f0(+0x44, the format at +0x24). Returns 1; 0 with SetLastError(14) when an allocation fails (both tables freed) or SetLastError(0x3eb) when 0042d7f0 does. ShellSound_Init calls it with sampleCount = fileCount + 10.

entries.name: Sfx_Construct
entries.description: (sfx): clears the file and sample tables (+0x34, +0x38), the voice counts (+0x3c, +0x40) and the bytes cached (+0x1c), sets defaults, and reads [Sound] from data\sound.cfg: Driver (read, then +0x2a set to 1 regardless), Buffers into +0x30 (atol, 1-64, else 5), Rate (atol of 11 giving +0x24 = 0x10 and anything else 0x20), and Width ('Mono', compared case-insensitively, giving +0x28 = 4 and anything else 8). +0x26 is fixed at 1 and +0x32 at 0x200. Increments the count at *Rtl_DtorCountPtr. Caller found by es2_xref: ShellSound_Init.

entries.name: ShellSoundManager_Dtor
entries.description: (manager, flags): Sos_Shutdown (which ends with Sos_UnbindLibrary), Mem_Delete on the arrays at +0x34 and +0x38 (clearing both), then Mem_Delete(manager) when flags bit 0 is set. ShellSound_Shutdown runs it on ShellSound_Manager with 3. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SfxManager_Dtor.

entries.name: ShellSound_ReleaseDriver
entries.description: Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver. ShellSound_Stop calls it between its two Mono_Printf marks.

entries.name: ShellSound_AcquireDriver
entries.description: Returns Sos_AcquireDigiDriver's answer. ShellSound_Start calls it.

entries.name: maybe_Sfx_FillDefaultsThunk
entries.description: (sfx, out): SFX-level thunk to maybe_Sfx_FillDefaults(out), the same guarded-call shape as Sfx_StopMusic. es2_xref finds no reference to it; DBSIM's copy (00463870) has none either.

entries.name: Sfx_SetMemoryCap
entries.description: (sfx, cap): with a non-zero cap below the current cap +0x18, Sfx_EvictForSpace(sfx, +0x18 - cap); when +0x18 is 0 and a non-zero cap is below the bytes cached +0x1c, Sfx_EvictForSpace(sfx, +0x1c - cap); then stores cap at +0x18. No caller found by es2_xref. Identical after normalisation to DBSIM's Sfx_SetMemoryCap (00463898).
entries.source: VSHELL disassembly at 0042c12a; diff against DBSIM 00463898

entries.name: Sfx_ServiceTimer
entries.description: (sfx, hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): returns Sos_Service(hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam); its guard on Sos_Service's address (MOV EAX,0x42d8b9; TEST EAX,EAX) always passes. No caller found by es2_xref. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sfx_ServiceTimer (004638e4).
entries.source: VSHELL disassembly at 0042c176; diff against DBSIM 004638e4

entries.name: Sfx_Open
entries.description: SFX::open (asserts 'SFX::open: Can not allocate a ...' in inc\sfx_fix.h, with SetLastError(14)): (sfx, name, mode, a, b). Takes a free 0x28-byte handle slot from the table at +0x38 (count +0x14), numbering it (serial +0x20 << 16) | index, and fills its defaults (flags +8 = 0, +0xc = 5, +0x14 = 100, +0x18 = 1, +0x1c = 0x8000, +0x20 = 0x10000); its +4 takes the data entry's handle. Reuses a loaded 0x21c-byte data entry with the same name from the table at +0x34 (count +0x10), bumping its reference count at +0x208, or takes a free one and fills it: +4 the name, +0x204 a, +0x208 reference count 1, +0x20c loaded 0, +0x210 b (the size Sfx_Cache uses when non-zero), +0x214 the backend object, null. Mode 0 sets flag 1 at +8, and mode 2 sets 0x1000 there for a new data entry only. Returns the handle, or -1 when either table is full. ShellSound_Init calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_Close
entries.description: SFX::close (asserts in .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle). Asserts the handle is valid and current in the voice table +0x38 (0x28-byte slots) and that its file handle (+4) is valid and current in the file table +0x34 (0x21c-byte records). Stops the voice with Sfx_Stop when it is playing (flag 0x100), decrements the file's reference count +0x208 and, when that reaches 0, Sfx_Cache(sfx, handle, 0) and frees the file slot (-1); then frees the voice slot (+0 and +4 set to -1). Sfx_PickEvictionVictim calls it (es2_xref: one CALL, at 0042ce47). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sfx_Close (00463b4c), whose asserts are compiled out.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042c3e3; diff against DBSIM 00463b4c

entries.name: Sfx_Cache
entries.description: SFX::cache (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, sampleHandle, load). Asserts the handle and its file handle are valid and current. A sample flagged 0x1000 returns 1 at once. Otherwise brings its file's loaded state (+0x20c) to load: unloading (only while the file's reference count +0x208 is below 2, else SetLastError(0x20)) frees it through 0042d906 and takes its size (+0x210) off the bytes cached (+0x1c); loading opens the file as a VolRStream (assert 'Unable to open file' otherwise), takes its size once (assert 'Bogus file size' for 0), makes room through 0042ce58 when the cache limit (+0x18) would be exceeded, and loads it through 0042d906. Returns the resulting loaded state. Sfx_Play calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_Play
entries.description: SFX::play (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle). Asserts on an invalid (-1) or stale handle, and on a sample whose file index is invalid or stale. Sample slots are 0x28 bytes at sfx+0x38 (the handle's low 16 bits index them; +4 the file index, +8 flags), sound files 0x21c bytes at sfx+0x34 (+4 the file name, +0x20c loaded). Loads the file when needed (Sfx_Cache), starts it (Sfx_StartVoice), counts it as a playing song (+0x40; flag bit 0, Sfx_StartVoice's MIDI path) or sample (+0x3c), sets the playing bit 0x100 and returns 1; returns 0 when loading or starting fails.

entries.name: Sfx_Stop
entries.description: SFX::stop (asserts in inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle). Asserts the handle is valid and current (its 0x28-byte slot in the array at sfx+0x38 holds the same handle); returns 1 at once when the slot's playing bit 0x100 is clear. Otherwise asserts the slot's file handle (+4) is valid and current in the 0x21c-byte file array at sfx+0x34 and runs Sfx_StopVoice. When that returns 0: SetLastError(0x3eb), the 'Drivers will not stop sample' assert and 0. Else decrements the playing-song (+0x40, flag bit 0) or playing-sample (+0x3c) count, clears the playing bit and returns 1. Sfx_EvictForSpace and two other functions call it. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sfx_Stop (00464014).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; es2_naming.py match/diff against the DBSIM function named in the description

entries.name: Sfx_IsDone
entries.description: SFX::isDone (asserts in .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle). Asserts the handle is valid and current. For a playing voice (flag 0x100) returns 0 while Sos_VoiceIsDone(slot + 4) reports 0, else stops it with Sfx_Stop; returns 1 otherwise. No caller found by es2_xref. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sfx_IsDone (004640e4), which tests the handle instead of asserting.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042cc1e; diff against DBSIM 004640e4

entries.name: Sfx_Service
entries.description: Sos_Service(0, 0, 0, 0): the library service call with no window message. 00404895 calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sfx_Service (0046415c).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042cce0; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0046415c

entries.name: Sfx_PickEvictionVictim
entries.description: (sfx): scores every live voice slot (the +0x14 slots of 0x28 bytes at +0x38 whose handle is not -1), asserting in .\inc\sfx_fix.h that its file handle is valid and current: priority +0xc, plus 100 when its file is cached (+0x20c), 1000 when playing (0x100) and 10000 when playing and looping (0x80). Takes the lowest score below 20000, closes that voice with Sfx_Close and returns its handle; returns -1 when every score is 20000 or more. No caller found by es2_xref. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sfx_PickEvictionVictim (0046417c), whose asserts are compiled out.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042ccfe; diff against DBSIM 0046417c

entries.name: Sfx_EvictForSpace
entries.description: (sfx, bytesNeeded): frees cached sound files until bytesNeeded are released. Scores each loaded file reference count * 10 + 1, plus for each of its sample slots the slot's +0xc, 1000 when it is playing (0x100) and 10000 more when it is also flagged 0x80; a file with a 0x1000 sample scores 0 and is never evicted. Then repeatedly takes the lowest non-zero score, stops every sample of the file through Sfx_Stop when the score is 1000 or more, frees it through Sos_LoadOrFreeSample and takes its size off the bytes cached (+0x1c). The free's MIDI flag comes from the last sample slot the scoring pass visited, not from the evicted file. Returns whether enough was freed. Sfx_Cache calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetCallback
entries.description: SFX::setCallback (asserts in .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, value). Asserts the handle is valid and current, then writes value to the voice slot's +0x10. No caller found by es2_xref. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sfx_SetCallback (004644d8), which skips the write for a bad handle instead of asserting.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042d0a3; diff against DBSIM 004644d8

entries.name: Sfx_SetVolume
entries.description: SFX::setVolume (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, volume). Asserts 'Can not setVolume an invalid handle' for handle -1 and 'Sample handle is old and no longer valid' when the handle does not match the one stored in its slot (the low 16 bits index 0x28-byte slots at sfx+0x38). Stores the volume at slot +0x14 and applies it now (Sos_ApplyVolume) when the slot is playing (+9 bit 0).

entries.name: Sfx_SetPitch
entries.description: SFX::setPitch (asserts in .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, pitch). Asserts the handle is valid and current; clears the voice's flag 0x400 for pitch 0x10000 and sets it otherwise, writes pitch to +0x20, and when the voice is playing (0x100) Sos_ApplyVoicePitch(slot + 4). No caller found by es2_xref. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sfx_SetPitch (00464568), which skips a bad handle instead of asserting.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042d1e3; DBSIM decompile at 00464568

entries.name: Sfx_SetPan
entries.description: SFX::setPan (asserts in .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, pan). Asserts the handle is valid and current; clears the voice's flag 0x800 for pan 0x8000 and sets it otherwise, writes pan to +0x1c, and when the voice is playing (0x100) Sos_ApplyVoicePan(slot + 4). No caller found by es2_xref. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sfx_SetPan (004645d8), which skips a bad handle instead of asserting.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042d2a9; DBSIM decompile at 004645d8

entries.name: Sfx_SetLooping
entries.description: SFX::setLooping (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, loops). Validates the handle like Sfx_Play, clears flag 0x80 for a count of 1 and sets it otherwise, stores the count at slot +0x18 and applies it now (0042dc6e) when the slot is playing.

entries.name: Sfx_SetPriority
entries.description: SFX::setPriority (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, priority). Asserts 'Can not setPriority an invalid handle' for handle -1 and 'Sample handle is old and no longer valid' when the handle differs from the one stored in its 0x28-byte voice slot (low 16 bits index the table at sfx+0x38), then stores priority at slot +0x0c. The asserting build of DBSIM's Sfx_SetPriority (004646b4), which skips the store instead of asserting. No caller found by es2_xref.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042d430; es2_naming diff against DBSIM 004646b4

entries.name: Sfx_GetAttributes
entries.description: SFX::getAttributes (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle). Asserts 'Can not getAttributes an invalid handle' for handle -1 and 'Sample handle is old and no longer valid' on a stale handle, then returns the voice slot's flags dword +8 (table sfx+0x38, stride 0x28). The asserting build of DBSIM's 004646e8, which returns 0 for a bad handle. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sfx_SetAttributes
entries.description: SFX::setAttributes (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, flags). Asserts 'Can not setAttributes an invalid handle' for handle -1 and 'Sample handle is old and no longer valid' on a stale handle, then writes flags to the voice slot's +8 (table sfx+0x38, stride 0x28) as given and returns. The asserting build of DBSIM's 00464720. No caller found by es2_xref.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042d545; es2_naming diff against DBSIM 00464720

entries.description: SFX::getSampleData (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle). Asserts 'Can not access an invalid handle' for handle -1 and 'Sample handle is old and no longer valid' on a stale handle, then returns a pointer to the voice slot +4 (table sfx+0x38, stride 0x28), the record the Sos_ voice functions take. The asserting build of DBSIM's Sfx_GetVoiceRecord (0046479c), which returns 0 for a bad handle. No caller found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sfx_StopAll
entries.description: SFX::stopAll (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx). For each sample slot with the playing bit 0x100, asserts its file handle is valid and current, stops it through 0042da8c and, when that succeeds, decrements the playing-song (+0x40, flag bit 0) or playing-sample (+0x3c) count and clears the playing bit. The loop runs over the first +0x10 slots of the sample table, +0x10 being the file count. ShellSound_Stop calls it.

entries.name: Str_FormatToStatic
entries.description: (format, ...): vsprintf into the static buffer 0048a840 and returns it. Sfx_Cache formats its assert messages with it.

entries.name: Sos_InitBackend
entries.description: (window, format): the VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sos_InitBackend: keeps window at Music_NotifyWindow, Sos_BindLibrary, copies format words 0, 1, 2, 6 and 7 (from the SFX's +0x24) into 00473174-0047317c, and opens the drivers through Sos_OpenDrivers with the configured driver id (word 3) and MIDI id 0xffff, then with id 1 and 0xffff, unbinding the library when both fail. Returns true on success. Caller found by es2_xref: Sfx_Init.

entries.description: Sos_ShutdownDrivers, then Sos_UnbindLibrary. ShellSoundManager_Dtor's first call. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_Shutdown.

entries.description: Returns whether Sos_AcquireDriver(Sos_GetDriverHandle()) returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_AcquireDigiDriver.

entries.description: Sos_ReleaseDriver(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), 0x1000). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver.

entries.name: Sos_Service
entries.description: (hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): Sos_UserService(Sos_GetDriverHandle()), then Sos_HandleWindowMessage with the message when hwnd is non-null. Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_Service (004736cc).

entries.name: maybe_Sfx_FillDefaults
entries.description: (out): writes {0x78, 0x20, 1} into three dwords at out (+0 = 0x78, +4 = 0x20, +8 = 1). What the three mean is not established. Reached only through maybe_Sfx_FillDefaultsThunk. Byte-identical to DBSIM's 00473700.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; es2_naming.py match/diff against the DBSIM function named in the description

entries.name: Sos_LoadOrFreeSample
entries.description: (file + 4, unused, load, isMidiSong): the VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sos_LoadOrFreeSample: loads (0042e47d digital, 0042e76c MIDI) or frees (0042e625, 0042e816) the file's backend object at file +0x214, nulling it on a free. Returns true on success. Sfx_Cache and Sfx_EvictForSpace call it.

entries.name: Sfx_StartVoice
entries.description: (file + 4, sample + 4): starts a cached sample. Flag bit 0 (sample +8) is a MIDI song: Sos_MidiInitSong on the file's loaded object (file +0x214), then Sos_MidiStartSong, uninitialising it on failure. Flag 0x1000 goes to 0042e846. Otherwise a digital sample: both channels' volume = volume (+0x14) * Sos_MasterVolume * 0x7fff / 10000, the loop count (+0x18) less 1 (-1, forever, for 0), and two further fields copied into the SOS sample header, then Sos_StartSample on Sos_GetDriverHandle() with the voice handle out at sample +0x24. Returns true on success. Sfx_Play calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_StopVoice
entries.description: (file + 4, sample + 4): stops a playing sample by its flags (sample +8): bit 0, a MIDI song, Sos_MidiStopSong and Sos_MidiUnInitSong; 0x1000, a stream, 0042eb13; otherwise Sos_StopSample on Sos_GetDriverHandle(). The voice handle is sample +0x24. Returns 1. Sfx_StopAll calls it.

entries.name: Sos_PauseVoice
entries.description: (voice): for a MIDI song (voice +4 bit 0) returns whether Sos_MidiPauseSong(+0x20, 0) answers 0; for a digital sample returns 0 (XOR EAX,EAX) without a call. No caller found by es2_xref. Exact match of DBSIM's 004738fc.
entries.source: VSHELL disassembly at 0042dae6; es2_naming match VSHELL DBSIM

entries.name: Sos_ResumeVoice
entries.description: (voice): for a MIDI song (voice +4 bit 0) returns whether Sos_MidiResumeSong(+0x20) answers 0; for a digital sample returns 0 without a call. No caller found by es2_xref. Exact match of DBSIM's 00473928.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042db0f; es2_naming match VSHELL DBSIM

entries.name: Sos_VoiceIsDone
entries.description: (voice): Sos_MidiSongDone(+0x20) for a MIDI song (flags +4 bit 0), otherwise Sos_SampleDone(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20). 0042cc1e asks it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_VoiceIsDone (00473950).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042db36; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00473950

entries.name: Sos_GetVoiceBytesProcessed
entries.description: (voice): for a digital sample (voice +4 bit 0 clear) returns Sos_GetBytesProcessed(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20); for a MIDI song returns 0. No caller found by es2_xref. Exact match of DBSIM's 00473980.

entries.name: Sos_SetMasterVolume
entries.description: (voice): writes Sos_MasterVolume from the record's +0x10. es2_xref.py finds no branch, stored pointer or vtable slot referencing it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_SetMasterVolume.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyMidiMasterVolume
entries.description: (voice): Sos_MidiSetMasterVolume((voice +0x10) * 0x7f / 100), the voice's 0-100 volume scaled to MIDI's 0-127; the MIDI branch of Sos_ApplyVolume on its own. No caller found by es2_xref. Identical after normalisation to DBSIM's 004739bc.

entries.name: Sos_OpenDrivers
entries.description: (digitalId, midiId, window, arg4): opens whichever SOS drivers are asked for and not yet open: MIDI detection first, then the digital driver (detect, Sos_InitSystem, Sos_TimerInitSystem, the format check against the detected capabilities with the 0x15 fallback, Sos_InitDriver into Sos_DriverHandle, Sos_SetActiveWindow, Sos_DigiDriverOpen set), then the MIDI driver into Sos_MidiDriverHandle, loading MELODIC.BNK and DRUM.BNK through Sos_LoadBankFile for driver type 0xa002 or 0xa009 with capability bit 2. Returns 0, or 1 / the capabilities | 0x1c0000 on failure with Sos_LastError set. Sos_InitBackend calls it twice. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_OpenDrivers (00473da0).

Returns 0.

entries.name: Sos_LoadWaveSample
entries.description: (path, out): opens path as a VolRStream (returns 1 when it will not open), GlobalAlloc(0x40, size + 0x100) (returns 1 on failure), reads the whole file to header +0x100, zeroes the first 0xfc bytes and keeps the handle at +0xfc. A file starting 'RIFF' (004731e9) is taken as a canonical WAV: data at file +0x2c, length +0x10 = the dword at file +0x28 less 0x2c, rate +0x38 from file +0x18, channels +0x40 from +0x16, bits +0x3c from +0x22, +0x44 = 0x8000 for 8-bit; anything else as raw 8-bit mono at 0x2b11 (11025) Hz, +0x44 = 0x8000. Then +0x48 = 0x8000, +0x30 = 0x7fff7fff, Sos_Prepare32Memory(data, file size, +4), *out = header, returns 0. Sos_LoadOrFreeSample's digital load. Identical after normalisation to DBSIM's Sos_LoadWaveSample (00474254).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042e47d; es2_naming diff against DBSIM 00474254

entries.name: Sos_FreeSample
entries.description: (sample): when non-null, Sos_UnPrepare32Memory(+4), then GlobalUnlock and GlobalFree of the handle at +0xfc. Returns 0. Sos_LoadOrFreeSample's digital free. Identical after normalisation to DBSIM's Sos_FreeSample (004743fc).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042e625; es2_naming diff against DBSIM 004743fc

entries.name: Sos_LoadBankFile
entries.description: (path, outMemory, outPrepared): reads the whole file through a VolRStream into GlobalAlloc'd memory and Sos_Prepare32Memory's it. Returns 0, or 1 when the file will not open or the allocation fails. Sos_OpenDrivers loads MELODIC.BNK and DRUM.BNK with it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_LoadBankFile (00474430).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; es2_naming.py match/diff against the DBSIM function named in the description

entries.name: Sos_FreePreparedMemory
entries.description: (memory, prepared): Sos_UnPrepare32Memory(prepared), then GlobalUnlock and GlobalFree of memory's global handle when memory is non-null. Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_FreePreparedMemory.

entries.name: Sos_LoadMidiSong
entries.description: (path, out): _lopen(path, 0) -- the plain file system, not a volume -- returning 1 when it fails; takes the size with _llseek, GlobalAlloc(0x40, size + 0x34) (returns 1 on failure), _hread's the file to header +0x24, zeroes the 0x20-byte header, keeps the handle at +0x20 and the data pointer at +0, then Sos_Prepare32Memory(data, size, +4) and Sos_Prepare32Memory(header, 0x20, +8), *out = header, returns 0. Sos_LoadOrFreeSample's MIDI-song load. DBSIM's Sos_LoadMidiSong (00474550) differs in one place: it passes header +0x24 directly where this reloads it from +0.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042e76c; es2_naming diff against DBSIM 00474550

entries.name: Sos_FreeSong
entries.description: (song): when non-null, Sos_UnPrepare32Memory on +4 and +8, then GlobalUnlock and GlobalFree of the handle at +0x20. Returns 0. Sos_LoadOrFreeSample's MIDI-song free. Identical after normalisation to DBSIM's Sos_FreeSong (004745fc).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042e816; es2_naming diff against DBSIM 004745fc

entries.name: Sos_StartFileStream
entries.description: (path, arg, handleOut): plays a file as an SOS stream: Sos_StreamAcquire with a raw 8-bit mono 11025 Hz header, opens the file with _lopen (the plain file system), reads eight 0x8000-byte buffers into GlobalAlloc'd memory, prepares and queues each that read anything (Sos_StreamPrepareBuffer, Sos_StreamAddBuffer) and Sos_StreamStart, storing the stream handle in *handleOut. Returns 0, or 1 when the stream, the file or an allocation fails. Sfx_StartVoice's path for a sample flagged 0x1000.

entries.name: Sos_RefillStreamBuffer
entries.description: (streamId, bufferHeader): _hread's up to 0x8000 bytes from the stream's file into the header's data (+2), stores the count at +0xe and, when it is non-zero, requeues the buffer with Sos_StreamAddBuffer. Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_RefillStreamBuffer (00474880).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042ead2; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00474880

entries.name: Sos_StopStream
entries.description: (streamId): Sos_StreamStop and Sos_StreamRelease, _lclose's the stream's file, then for each of its eight buffers Sos_StreamUnPrepareBuffer, Sos_UnPrepare32Memory on both prepared handles and GlobalUnlock/GlobalFree. Returns 0. Sfx_StopVoice and Sos_HandleWindowMessage call it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_StopStream (004748c4).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042eb13; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 004748c4

entries.name: Sos_HandleWindowMessage

Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_HandleWindowMessage (00474994).

entries.name: ShellSound_Init
entries.description: Creates the shell's sound manager at 004731f0 unless -s cleared Shell_SoundEnabled: loads hmi\gm_69.wav (press), hmi\bptlt2.wav (tab click), hmi\lswitch2.wav (startup switch) and hmi\shell1.wav or shell2.wav by option 5, flips option 5 and saves prefs.cfg, sets the music looping forever at the music volume.

entries.name: ShellSound_PlayTabClick
entries.description: The tab click, hmi\bptlt2.wav at volume 100, gated as ShellSound_PlayPress. The last call of each of the eight tab handlers.

entries.name: ShellSound_PlayPress
entries.description: The press sound, hmi\gm_69.wav at volume 100, while the manager exists, SOUNDS (option 1) is on and the sounds are running. ESButtonFont_HandleEvent, ESButtonBitmap_HandleEvent and ESRadioButton_HandleEvent call it on a press.

entries.name: ShellSound_PlaySwitch
entries.description: hmi\lswitch2.wav at volume 100, gated as the press sound. Called once, by the startup sequence widget's handler 004311b8 on its first tick.

entries.name: ShellSound_Start
entries.description: Unless the sounds are running: raises 00473200, sets the music looping forever, plays the press sound at volume 0 and starts the music at the music volume. Startup, the movie queue's end, and WM_SETFOCUS.

entries.name: ShellSound_Stop
entries.description: While the sounds are running: sets the music to play once, stops every sound, gives up the driver focus and drops 00473200. Before the movie queue, WM_KILLFOCUS, ONLINE MANUAL and the stage-5 location movie.

entries.name: ShellSound_Shutdown
entries.description: ShellSound_Stop, then destroys the sound manager and clears 004731f0. Called by Shell_ShutdownDevicesAndSound and by the insert-CD failure in Movie_PlayQueue.

entries.name: ShellSound_FadeOut
entries.description: While MUSIC (option 0) is on, steps the music volume down one each time more than 10 ms of GetTickCount have passed, pumping messages, until it is below 2.

entries.name: ShellSound_FadeIn
entries.description: While MUSIC (option 0) is on, steps the music volume up one each time more than 10 ms of GetTickCount have passed, pumping messages, until it is past 99.

entries.name: ShellSound_Stop_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to ShellSound_Stop. OnlineManual_Open calls it.

entries.name: ShellSound_Start_Thunk
entries.description: CALL ShellSound_Start; RET. MainWndProc's WM_SETFOCUS (7) case calls it when Avi_Playing is clear, after setting Shell_HasFocus; ShellSound_Stop_Thunk (0042f287) is the WM_KILLFOCUS counterpart directly before it.

entries.name: Shell_BuildSimArgv
entries.description: Frameless code, after the SFX class record. Returns at once unless ShellSwitch_L and Shell_GetExitCode() are both nonzero; then Display_ReleaseDirectDraw when DAT_0046d740 is set, Mem_NewArray(0x40), and fills it with pointers to 'dummy', '-eggplant', '-Z' (DAT_0046d740 clear), '-s' (Shell_SoundEnabled clear), '-v3', '-h', '-F' (Shell_Language 1), '-G' (Shell_Language 2), '-m' (ShellSwitch_M set), '-D' (ShellSwitch_D nonzero) and a final empty string (0047332d), and returns the count before it with the array pointer dropped. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: CellWalk_SetCallback
entries.description: (ctx, callback, value): stores the cell walk's callback at ctx+0x14 and its value at ctx+0x18.

entries.name: CellWalk_Polygon
entries.description: (ctx, centre, polygon): cuts the polygon into four quadrants around the centre cell with Poly_ClipToHalfPlane, scan-converts each with Poly_BuildSpanList, and calls ctx's callback(ctx, row, xFrom, xTo) per row run, far to near when maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled == 0 && DAT_00471884 != 0 (the image values) and near to far otherwise. hgrid.cpp's cell renderer 00429b4a calls it.

entries.name: Point_RotateQuarterAbout
entries.description: (&x, &y, centre): x' = cx + (y - cy), y' = cy - (x - cx), in place. CellWalk_PolygonByColumn turns its polygon with it.

entries.name: Point_UnrotateQuarterAbout
entries.description: (&x, &y, centre): the inverse of Point_RotateQuarterAbout, x = cx - (y' - cy), y = cy + (x' - cx), in place.

entries.name: CellWalk_PolygonByColumn
entries.description: (ctx, centre, polygon): CellWalk_Polygon's far-to-near walk by column: turns the points a quarter turn about the centre (Point_RotateQuarterAbout), walks, turns each run's end cells back (Point_UnrotateQuarterAbout) and calls callback(ctx, column, yFrom, yTo), then turns the points back. Ghidra's decompile misreads its context as Rtl_VectorNew's return; it is the first argument, held in EDI.

entries.name: CellWalk_Rect
entries.description: (ctx, centre, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): the far-to-near cell walk over a rectangle, no scan conversion, each half running its first quadrant's rows before its second's.

entries.name: Poly_BuildSpanList
entries.description: (poly, spans, header): poly is {count, int32 {x, y} points*}. Translates the points in place so their minimum x and y are 0 (and does not translate them back), scan-converts them into spans with Poly_ScanConvertEitherWinding, adds the minimum x back to every span, and fills header = {top row, bottom row, row count, pointer to spans + 8 (the first {x0, x1} pair)} with rows in screen coordinates. CellWalk_Polygon and CellWalk_PolygonByColumn call it on each quadrant Poly_ClipToHalfPlane cuts.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00465e0a and its two entry wrappers; DBSIM copies matched by byte comparison

entries.name: Poly_ClipToHalfPlane
entries.description: (keepHigh, alongX, value, in, out): one Sutherland-Hodgman pass keeping the part of polygon in ({count, points*}) with x (alongX) or y at >= value (keepHigh) or <= value, points on the line kept, into out (whose point pointer the caller sets); crossings computed from the previous point, truncating. Returns the count's low byte. The case bodies sit behind a jump table Ghidra left undisassembled.

entries.name: Stats_ScanSlots
entries.description: stats.cpp. Fills the eleven-entry slot summary table at 0048cddc by opening every save the directory marks in use and seeking block by block to the pilot record, the salvage pool and the career position. Its skip counts are a second independent statement of the whole GAME_?.SAV block order.

entries.name: Stats_StageCurrentGame
entries.description: Writes one slot's summary from the live game rather than from a file: the player's pilot record fields copied one at a time out of 00482a7c, then CareerSalvage, the campaign stage and the mission. This is what binds each summary offset to a named pilot-record offset.

entries.name: MainMenu_BuildScreen
entries.description: wmain.cpp. Builds the main menu once at shell startup: the six-frame bay2a_80..84 startup widget (StartupAnimWidget), the backdrop root (DAT_0048d0c8), the MAIN MENU TitledPanel {0x90,0xad,0x1e2,0x138} (DAT_0048d0cc) and its ten buttons in two columns.

entries.name: MainMenu_Show
entries.description: Tab 0's entry: shows the main menu's root (DAT_0048d0c8) and panel (DAT_0048d0cc), then writes the greying trio at CONTINUE GAME (DAT_0048d0d4) from 00482a19, slot 10's in-use byte.

entries.name: MainMenu_Hide
entries.description: Hides the main menu's root and panel. Called first by every main-menu button that leaves the menu.

entries.name: StartupAnim_OnTick
entries.description: Handler of the startup sequence widget (StartupAnimWidget), run on every alarm tick: plays ShellSound_PlaySwitch on its first run (DAT_00473608) and, once the widget's +0x6d reaches 5, hides it and calls MainMenu_Show, once only (DAT_00473604); with Shell_PerformanceNotePending set also puts up the Performance Note message box.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnInstantAction
entries.description: INSTANT ACTION's handler: InstantAction_Active = 1, Shell_SetCampaignMode(0), InstantAction_SelectDemo, blank (full screen) or palette scope show/hide, Game_NewCareer("TRAINEE", option 0x27), Game_ExportMissionHandoff, Shell_SetExitCode(2), Shell_QuitFlag = 1.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnStartNewGame
entries.description: START NEW GAME's handler: MainMenu_Hide, Shell_SetCampaignMode(1), Registration_Show.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnContinue
entries.description: CONTINUE GAME's handler: Game_LoadSlot(10, 1), selected save slot 10, then the bare frame when DAT_0048260e is 2, otherwise EndOfGame_Show(DAT_0048260e).

entries.name: MainMenu_OnSaveRestore
entries.description: SAVE/RESTORE's handler: MainMenu_Hide, campaign mode 1 (Shell_SetCampaignMode), SaveScreen_ExitTarget = 0, SaveScreen_Enter.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnPreferences
entries.description: PREFERENCES' handler: MainMenu_Hide, PreferencesScreen_Enter.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnViewDemo
entries.description: VIEW DEMO's handler: Shell_BlankScreen when full screen, Shell_SetExitCode(5), Shell_QuitFlag = 1.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnCredits
entries.description: CREDITS' handler: shows the bare window DAT_0048d0c4, plays movie 0x54 through Movie_Enqueue and Movie_PlayQueue, hides it.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnQuit
entries.description: QUIT's handler: Shell_QuitFlag = 1, Shell_BlankScreen.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnOnlineManual
entries.description: ONLINE MANUAL's handler: OnlineManual_Open.

entries.name: OnlineManual_Open
entries.description: Leaves full screen, option 6 = 0, commit, save all, ShellSound_Stop, then Shell_OpenHelp on Path_UnderDriveCfg(<language>\es2guide.hlp), the folder chosen by Shell_ReadLanguageCfg's letter E/F/G; any other letter fails a severity-4 assert, 'online help not found', and Assert_Report exits the shell.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnPracticeMissions
entries.description: PRACTICE MISSIONS' handler: MainMenu_Hide, PracticeScreen_Show, Shell_SetCampaignMode(0).

entries.name: QuitAlert_Build
entries.description: Builds the Alt+F4 (key code 0x23e) QUIT alert QuitAlert (0048d0fc): caption estext 0x12 QUIT, buttons 0x11 CANCEL (QuitAlert_OnCancel) and 0x10 ACCEPT (QuitAlert_OnAccept).

entries.name: QuitAlert_OnCancel
entries.description: The QUIT alert's CANCEL button handler.

entries.name: QuitAlert_OnAccept
entries.description: The QUIT alert's ACCEPT handler: sets Shell_QuitFlag.

entries.name: InsertCdPanel_Build
entries.description: Builds the insert-CD panel Movie_PlayQueue shows when a non-intro movie will not open: a Window over the root window's rect (InsertCdPanel, InsertCdPanel (0048d108)), an ESAlert {0xcf, 0xcb, 0x1b4, 0x12a} in it captioned estext 0x153 'Insert CD into CD Drive' (font ShellFont2HandleB, border 0x15; +0x55 = 0x25, +0x65 = 1, +0x6d = 0x31, +0x71 = 0xb3) at InsertCdAlert (0048d10c), and two ESButtonFont buttons, 0x154 'Continue' {0x41, 0x25, 0xa3, 0x34} (InsertCdPanel_OnContinue) and 0x155 'Quit' {0x41, 0x3b, 0xa3, 0x4a} (InsertCdPanel_OnQuit), border 0x22, at 0048d110 and 0048d114. Alert_Show, then hides the panel. Shell_BuildScreensAndStart calls it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00431c18; estext.bin ENG ids 0x153-0x155

entries.name: InsertCdPanel_OnContinue
entries.description: (event): the insert-CD panel's Continue handler: hides InsertCdPanel (0048d108), sets InsertCdPanel_Continue (00473b30) to 1, and deletes the event (vtable +0x18 with 3). Movie_PlayQueue's wait loop ends on that flag, clears it and retries the movie. InsertCdPanel_Build passes it to ESButtonFont_Ctor (stored pointer at 00431d89).

entries.name: InsertCdPanel_OnQuit
entries.description: (event): the insert-CD panel's Quit handler: sets Shell_QuitFlag and deletes the event (vtable +0x18 with 3), leaving the panel up. Movie_PlayQueue's wait loop ends on Shell_QuitFlag and it returns. InsertCdPanel_Build passes it to ESButtonFont_Ctor (stored pointer at 00431e12).

entries.name: Repair_InstallHotspotHandlers
entries.description: Fills RepairHotspotHandlers' 25 slots with the thunks Repair_OnHotspot00..Repair_OnInternalRow8. Repair_BuildScreen's first call.

entries.name: Repair_BuildScreen
entries.description: Builds every widget of tab 3, REPAIR: eight per-bay damage grids over {0x10,0x2f,0xe0,0x12f}, the content TitledPanel {0xf1,0x2b,0x278,0x1d9}, the External and Internal list panels with their 16 and 9 rows, the mode and salvage readouts, three FramedPanel readout panels with REPAIR / REPAIR ALL / SCRAP, and CANCEL. Opens no file; every rect is four immediates on its own stack.

entries.name: Repair_Enter
entries.description: Brings the repair screen up: shows the content panel and both list panels, sets the mode readout from ShellOption_RepairMode, calls Squad_SelectBay(Herc_FirstBuiltBay) when the current bay holds nothing workable -- before TabHandler_Repair stores 3, so that call takes the previous tab's arm, fills both lists (00433caf), snapshots the pool and the machine (Repair_Snapshot, 004338f6) and seeds the selection at (0, 0).

entries.name: Repair_Leave
entries.description: Tab 3's teardown, reached from the dispatcher at 00439ea7: hides the content panel and both list panels. Counterpart of Repair_Enter (004332ec).

entries.name: Repair_HotspotCategory
entries.description: (column, row) to condition-array category: 1 for any non-zero column, 2 for column 0 rows above 5, else 0. These are the same three modes HercStatus_Get takes -- 0 external group, 1 internal, 2 hardpoint.

entries.name: Repair_HotspotIndex
entries.description: Index within the category: row minus 6 for category 2, otherwise row.

entries.name: Repair_RefreshDetail
entries.description: Refills the three readout panels from the selection: the selected component's one-level repair cost (Repair_SelectionCost, 00411454), its condition word and colour, Repair_HercCost(herc, 100), and CareerSalvage minus Armory_QueuedTotal, all suffixed estext 0xc8 'kg'. Then writes the greying trio at REPAIR, REPAIR ALL and SCRAP -- the first two on affordability, SCRAP on there being a machine that is not the last deployable one.

entries.name: Repair_RefreshSalvage
entries.description: The repair screen's salvage readout: CareerSalvage - Armory_QueuedTotal().

entries.name: Repair_Snapshot
entries.description: Copies CareerSalvage into RepairSnapshotSalvage and, with a bay selected, the selected machine's 66-byte status block (HercList_CopySelectedStatus) into RepairSnapshotStatus. Called at the end of Repair_Enter and of Squad_SelectBay's repair arm; Repair_OnCancel restores both.

entries.name: Repair_SwapDiagram
entries.description: Swaps the two per-bay pictures as the selection crosses between columns: the internals diagram (RepairInternalsPictures) is shown while the internals list is selected and the exploded external picture (0048d4bc) while column 0 is.

entries.name: Repair_FillRow
entries.description: Fills one (column, row) of the repair lists: reads the condition through HercStatus_Get, formats it '%d%%' into the row's fourth text child in the damage band's colour, and for a hardpoint row also writes the fitted weapon's name (estext 0x7e + id, or 0x7d --Empty--) and the one-based mount number. A row past the machine's mount capacity is blanked to estext entry 1.

entries.name: Repair_FillAllRows
entries.description: Calls Repair_FillRow over column 0's sixteen rows and column 1's nine, then Repair_RefreshDetail.

entries.name: Repair_SetComponentNames
entries.description: Writes the fifteen component names into the two lists' name columns from one of two fifteen-entry estext index tables, at 00474000 for a walker and 0047401e when the machine's chassis type is 8, the Razor. Called only from Squad_SelectBay's repair arm (0043d753); a bay change on another tab, and Repair_Enter's reselection (which runs under the previous tab's arm), leave the names as they were.

entries.name: Repair_ColorRow
entries.description: Repaints one repair list row in a colour pair -- called as (column, row, 0x10, 0x27) for the outgoing selection and (column, row, 0x29, 0x29) for the incoming. It writes the row Panel's border at +0x4d and its first text child's ink, indexing the sixteen widgets at 0048d140 for column 0 and the nine at 0048d184 for column 1, so this is what maps a (column, row) back to the widget that draws it.

entries.name: Repair_SelectHotspot
entries.description: Takes (column, row), returns early if that pair is already selected, refuses a hardpoint row past the machine's mount capacity (+0x4c) or with nothing fitted, then repaints old and new, stores the pair and its resolved category and index, and refreshes the panel.

entries.name: Repair_OnContentPanelNoOp
entries.description: (event): its whole body deletes the event (vtable +0x18 with 3). Repair_BuildScreen passes it as the handler of the repair screen's content TitledPanel {0xf1, 0x2b, 0x278, 0x1d9}, estext 0x3d 'REPAIR' (RepairContentPanel (0048d138); stored pointer at 00432143), so a click on the panel is discarded, as Window_DispatchCallback discards one for a widget whose handler slot +0x3d is 0.

entries.name: Repair_OnExternalListNoOp
entries.description: (event): its whole body deletes the event (vtable +0x18 with 3). Repair_BuildScreen passes it as the handler of the external list's TitledPanel {4, 0x1a, 0xe5, 0x105}, estext 0x3e 'External', inside the content panel (RepairExternalList (0048d13c); stored pointer at 004321f1).
